minutes.headline: Planning Board approved the 50 and 52 Page Street plan and free GIS hours for Conservation; parking rules tabled.
minutes.summary: The board approved a plan changing property lines at 50 and 52 Page Street, approved prior minutes, and let the Conservation Commission use the free regional-planning GIS hours. Committee reports covered the high TCP cost estimate and the capital policy threshold, and a member voiced strong frustration over the sparsely attended, unrecorded Green Leaf cannabis community meeting. The parking workshop on the subdivision rules was tabled after the board leaned toward by-right uses set by the zoning official and site plan uses set by the planning board.

The capital planning committee is discussing whether the threshold for what counts as capital should change, and where small departments would get the money.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the population study cost and the remaining money for two master plan chapters; the free GIS hours would not make or break them.
MRPC is helping the town close out its existing award and reapply.

Parking table tabled to a later meeting; director to draft by-right uses as set by the zoning official and site plan uses set by the planning board, and add child care.
Applicant to sign mylars at the office once three signatures are gathered.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved, 4-0 by roll call, a plan changing the property lines at 50 and 52 Page Street.
The board voted 4-0 to let the Conservation Commission use the free annual regional-planning GIS hours.
The parking table workshop was tabled; the director will draft by-right uses set by the zoning official and site plan uses set by the board, and add child care.
A hearing on the subdivision regulation amendments will be scheduled for the first or second March meeting, probably the second.
A committee report put the preliminary building design estimate near the cost of a new build, and a member doubted town meeting would accept it.

why_it_matters: The building cost estimate and the discussion of the capital threshold bear on what town meeting may be asked to fund, and so on future tax bills.
The subdivision and parking rule changes will go to a public hearing, which is the point where residents can comment on what is allowed by right and what needs site plan review.
watch_next: A hearing on the subdivision regulation amendments, expected at the first or second March meeting, probably the second.
The revised parking table, with by-right and site plan uses and child care added, at a later meeting.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the two main votes, the main figures and the quorum, but differ on the GIS vote record, the capital threshold, and some decisions. The key point: the official minutes' GIS motion quote ends at "seconded for discussion" with no vote shown, and the official minutes list a $30,000 proposed threshold that ours does not.
